sections.content: In Hungarian, when stating where a country, region, or city is located, the existential verb *van / vannak* is strictly required: *Magyarország Közép-Európában van* (unlike predicate adjectives or professions, where *van* drops in the 3rd person: *Magyarország szép*). At B1, formal and civic texts elevate beyond simple *van* to precise geographical verbs such as *elhelyezkedik* ("is situated"), *fekszik* ("lies / is located"), and *terül el* ("extends / spreads out").

sections.title: Formal geographical verbs of location
rows: is situated, is located (geopolitical / formal register)
lies, is situated (natural terrain, borders, rivers)
extends, spreads out (broad regions, plains, landscapes)
can be found, is located (institutional / administrative)

items.spanish: Magyarország a Kárpát-medence szívében helyezkedik el.
items.english: Hungary is situated in the heart of the Carpathian Basin.

items.spanish: Az ország teljesen szárazföldi állam, közvetlen tengerpart nélkül.
items.english: The country is a landlocked state, without direct coastline.

items.spanish: A termékeny síkság a Duna és a Tisza mentén terül el.
items.english: The fertile plain extends along the Danube and the Tisza.

items.spanish: A Kárpát-medencét északról és keletről hegykoszorú védi.
items.english: The Carpathian Basin is protected by a ring of mountains from the north and east.

sections.content: When framing an answer in a citizenship interview, combine a precise verb like *helyezkedik el* with descriptive locative cases (*-ban/-ben*, *-on/-en/-ön*) and participial phrases: *A Közép-Európában fekvő Magyarország...* ("Hungary, lying in Central Europe..."). This instantly signals a natural B1 communicative competence.
